newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TOTTENHAM GAIN UPPER HAND IN JUNINHO BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOTTENHAM GAIN UPPER HAND IN JUNINHO BATTLE.

text.p: Tottenham appeared to have gained the upper hand in their battle with Atletico Madrid to sign Brazilian midfielder Juninho when his current club Middlesbrough said on Tuesday they were involved in negotiations only with the English premier league side.
"We've accepted a written bid from Tottenham for 11 million pounds ($18.3 milion)," said Dave Allen, Middlesbrough's public relations officer.
"It depends on whether he can agree personal terms with Spurs. It's up to him and Spurs to get together."

Middlesbrough's stance on the tug of war over Juninho came despite a report in the daily Spanish sports newspaper "Marca" that Juninho's father, who is also his personal manager, had agreed a move to Atletico Madrid.
Marca reported that Atletico's director general Miguel Angel Gil had agreed a fee of 12 million pounds with Middlesbrough chairman Steve Gibson during a telephone conversation.
But Middlesbrough said the only offer they had accepted was from Tottenham, though nothing was settled yet.
"He's a Middlesbrough player at the moment," said Allen. "He certainly hasn't signed for Tottenham."

Middlesbrough, who rejected what they termed a "derisory" offer from Atletico some weeks ago, hold the key to the Brazilian midfielder's future as he is still contracted to them for a further two years.

But Juninho is keen to leave Middlesbrough after the team were relegated from the premier league last season. He is understood to favour a move to Spain where he feels greater exposure on television in Brazil will increase his chances of making the national squad for the 1998 World Cup finals.

Allen dismissed a report in Britain's Sun newspaper that Juninho would move to Tottenham for one season, while Middlesbrough attempted to win back their premier league place, and then return to see out his contract.
"There is no truth in that," he said.
